Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal

S No directions and  Registrar's order  with Signatures  13.06.2024 WPCRL No. 606 of 2024  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. Akshay Pradhan, learned counsel along with Ms. Shalini Thakral, learned counsel for the petitioners and Mr. V.K. Jemini, learned Deputy Advocate General for the State.

2. By the instant writ petition, the petitioners are praying for quashing of FIR No. 046 of 2024 dated 16.01.2024, wherein the petitioners have been implicated for the offences punishable under Sections 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act read with Sections 323, 354, 498A, 504 and 506 of IPC, P.S. Laksar,
District Haridwar.

3. It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioners that the marriage of respondent No. 3 was solemnized on 20.04.2021 with Balwan son of Suresh Pal, who lodged a First Information Report on 07.01.2024 at P.S. Jathlana District Yamuna Nagar, bearing FIR No. 0007 of 2024,
wherein, in total five persons have been implicated including Meena (respondent No. 3), the daughter of the complainant and in counterblast to this, respondent No. 3 lodged the impugned FIR implicating the petitioners and two unknown persons.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the allegations as alleged are completely false and this is nothing but a case of glaring example of malicious prosecution which is evident from the facts that earlier to this FIR, on 07.01.2024, the father-in-law of the respondent No. 3 lodged the FIR No. 0007 of 2024 for the offences punishable under Sections 148, 149, 323, 452 and 506 of IPC.
5.

It is further submitted that the petitioners are the uncle, aunty and cousin brother of the husband of the complainant and have no nexus with the matrimonial discord in between the husband and the respondent/complainant.

6. Mr. V.K. Jemini, learned Deputy Advocate General accepts notice for respondent Nos. 1 & 2.
7.

Issue notice to respondent No. 3.
WPCRL/606/2024 on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199554691/

1 8. Learned counsel for the petitioners within a week, by registered post acknowledgement due,
returnable within three weeks.

In the meantime, the investigation pursuant to the FIR, bearing FIR No. 046 of 2024 dated 16.01.2024, P.S. Laksar, District Haridwar, may go on; however, the petitioners shall not be arrested provided they cooperate with the investigation.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 13.06.2024 Mahinder/
